title: Using third-party images: databases ready in seconds

videos.script: Most of what you run in containers was packaged by somebody else. A database, a cache, a queue. This lesson is about reading those images well enough to trust them and configure them. {{who}} First, who published it, and what the image does when it starts. {{run}} Then a configured Postgres in one command: a password, a database, a setup script, a volume and a port. {{ready}} And a trap. Postgres says it is ready, and the first connection fails anyway. On its first start the image runs the server twice, and the first one is only for setup. {{once}} Then a second trap: the setup runs once. A new password on the second start is silently ignored. {{more}} And last, two versions of Postgres and a Redis cache, side by side, with nothing installed.
